I lost $4,800 making three mistakes that most beginners repeat. Here's what cost me thousands so you can avoid it: 1. Not documenting my failures I'd run a test, it would fail, and I'd just move on to the next product.  No notes, no analysis. Three weeks later I'd make the exact same mistake with a different product and lose another $200. I burned $1,500 repeating the same targeting errors and creative mistakes because I had no system to track what I'd already tried.  When I finally started keeping a simple spreadsheet—product, spend, metrics, and why it failed—I stopped repeating expensive mistakes. The lesson: Document every test. If you're not learning from your losses, you're paying to make the same mistakes on repeat. 2. Not understanding my metrics I'd see CTR, CPC, ROAS in my ads manager and have no idea what was good versus bad. My CTR would be 0.8% and I'd think it was fine. It wasn't—that's terrible for dropshipping. I'd spend $300 with no sales and couldn't tell if my creative, targeting, product, or landing page was the problem.  I was operating blind. The lesson: Learn benchmark metrics for dropshipping. If you can't read your data, you're gambling with your ad budget. 3. Waiting too long to get a mentor I thought I could figure everything out from YouTube.  Getting a mentor can help you save yourself from stupid mistakes that can cost you time and money. The lesson: A good mentor saves you more than they cost. I spent $2,000 learning the hard way when $500 in guidance would've avoided most of it. Bottom line: Document your failures, understand your metrics, and get help early. These three things would've saved me thousands. This is how dropshipping actually works: First, you create your online store. You can do this with Shopify for $1/month. I also recommend connecting it to pagepilot.ai so you can just have AI design the store for you. Next, you sign up for Zendrop and link it to Shopify. Zendrop is your supplier. Essentially, they stock the product you're selling on your store. Then, when somebody buys the product on your store, Zendrop is notified, and they package up the product and ship it to your customer. You don't have to touch the product once. This way, you don't have to spend thousands buying a bunch of inventory. You only pay Zendrop once the customer has paid you first. #ecom #entrepreneur #business #shopify #onlinebusiness
